items.name: Ordinary ideal class group
items.statement: For a number field K with ring of integers O_K, Cl(K) is the multiplicative group of nonzero fractional O_K-ideals modulo nonzero principal fractional ideals.
items.locator: Introduction p.1 and §2 p.4, Taniguchi 2017-02-18 copy
items.note: Inherited from #1636: ClassGroup uses invertible fractional ideals; the Dedekind-domain instance for O_K gives the stated carrier. Not the narrow class group. Declaration statement reread at the prescribed Mathlib pin by codex-c83e7a. API: Use ClassGroup (O_K), mk0, equality modulo principal ideals and the kernel of squaring; import the quotient carrier. Tests: (1) Q has trivial class group; (2) principal nonzero ideals map to one; (3) ordinary versus narrow classes are distinguished.

items.name: Finiteness of the number-field class group
items.statement: For every number field K, the ordinary ideal class group Cl(O_K) is finite; its cardinality is h(K).
items.locator: Introduction p.1, implicit in h_m(K); §6 p.10
items.note: Inherited from #1636. Finiteness does not supply a degree-uniform torsion estimate. Declaration statement reread at the prescribed Mathlib pin by codex-c83e7a.

items.name: Archimedean absolute values
items.statement: M_infinity(K) consists of the archimedean absolute values associated to embeddings K → C; at a complex place use the ordinary complex modulus, not its square.
items.note: Inherited from #1636. Complex places have multiplicity two in the product formula and norm/volume computations. Declaration statement reread at the prescribed Mathlib pin by codex-c83e7a. API: Evaluate the existing absolute values, real/complex subtype tests, extension of embeddings and the norm product with multiplicities. Tests: (1) Q has one real place; (2) Q(i) has one complex place with multiplicity two; (3) conjugate embeddings define the same place.

items.name: Integral discriminant and its absolute value
items.statement: For a number field K, discr(K) is the determinant of the trace pairing on an integral basis; it is nonzero and independent of that basis. Write D_K = |discr(K)|.
items.note: Inherited from #1636. The Lean integer discr is signed; use its absolute value in all real powers. Declaration statement reread at the prescribed Mathlib pin by codex-c83e7a. API: Use signed discr and D=|discr|, integral-basis invariance, positivity of D and order-index comparisons as separate lemmas. Tests: (1) Q has D=1; (2) Q(i) has signed discriminant -4; (3) a nonmaximal order can have larger discriminant.

items.name: Minkowski space with one complex embedding per pair
items.statement: If K has r real and s complex places, embed K into R^r × C^s via its real embeddings and one representative of each complex pair. This real space has dimension n = [K:Q] = r + 2s.
items.note: Inherited from #1636. Use ordinary product measure and explicitly specify the Euclidean norm for successive minima, not the default product sup norm. Declaration statement reread at the prescribed Mathlib pin by codex-c83e7a. API: Import mixedEmbedding and its Euclidean transport; expose injectivity, real dimension and archimedean coordinate projections. Tests: (1) dimension r+2s equals n; (2) Q(i) contributes two real coordinates; (3) default product norm is not silently the Euclidean norm.

items.name: Covolume of the ring of integers
items.statement: In R^r × C^s with ordinary product Lebesgue measure, the mixed embedding of O_K has covolume 2^(-s) sqrt(D_K).
items.note: Inherited from #1636. Do not reuse this constant unchanged for a metric weighting complex coordinates by two. Declaration statement reread at the prescribed Mathlib pin by codex-c83e7a.

items.name: Covolume of a fractional ideal
items.statement: For a nonzero fractional ideal J of O_K, covol(mixedEmbedding(J)) = N_abs(J) 2^(-s) sqrt(D_K). For J = I^(-1) this is 2^(-s) sqrt(D_K)/N(I).
items.note: Inherited from #1636. The Lean input is a unit of the fractional-ideal monoid; the inverse case also uses multiplicativity of absolute norm. Declaration statement reread at the prescribed Mathlib pin by codex-c83e7a.

items.name: Minkowski convex-body theorem, strict volume form
items.statement: Let E be a finite-dimensional real normed space with additive Haar measure μ, and L a countable additive subgroup with measurable fundamental domain F. A convex symmetric set S with μ(F) 2^(dim E) < μ(S) contains a nonzero point of L.
items.note: Inherited from #1636. The strict theorem alone does not justify a boundary equality. Declaration statement reread at the prescribed Mathlib pin by codex-c83e7a.

items.name: Minkowski convex-body theorem, compact boundary form
items.statement: In a nontrivial finite-dimensional real normed space with additive Haar measure, a compact convex symmetric set S with μ(F) 2^(dim E) ≤ μ(S) contains a nonzero point of a countable discrete subgroup L with fundamental domain F.
items.locator: §2 p.4, boundary case of the non-strict bound
items.note: Inherited from #1636. Compactness, discreteness and nontriviality are required. Declaration statement reread at the prescribed Mathlib pin by codex-c83e7a.

items.name: Minkowski ideal-class representative bound
items.statement: Every class of a degree-n number field of signature (r,s) contains a nonzero integral ideal I with N(I) ≤ (4/pi)^s (n!/n^n) sqrt(D_K).
items.note: Inherited from #1636. This does not itself bound all archimedean values of a generator of I^m. Declaration statement reread at the prescribed Mathlib pin by codex-c83e7a.

items.name: Successive minima
items.statement: For a full lattice Λ in a positive-dimensional Euclidean real space with closed unit ball B, λ_i is the infimum of t > 0 such that Λ ∩ tB spans a real subspace of dimension at least i, for 1 ≤ i ≤ n.
items.locator: Theorems 1.6 and 3.1, pp.3,5; expanded standard definition
items.note: Inherited from #1636: reviewed AUDIT-02 distinguishes these planned definitions and the second theorem from existing Minkowski-first machinery. API: Infimum of radii containing i independent lattice vectors; positivity, monotonicity, attainment and Minkowski second product estimates. Tests: (1) rank-one lattice aZ has minimum |a|; (2) rectangular rank-two lattice has distinct minima; (3) zero-dimensional case has an empty product.

items.name: Weighted box and polydisc for a torsion ideal
items.statement: Given K of degree n, m ≥ 1, a nonzero integral ideal I and I^m = (α) with α ≠ 0, set R_v = D_K^(1/(2n)) |α|_v^(-1/m). The product of real intervals [-R_v,R_v] and closed complex discs of radius R_v is compact, symmetric and convex, with volume 2^r pi^s sqrt(D_K)/N(I).
items.note: A complex disc contributes pi R_v². The body volume is at least 2^n covol(I^(-1)), since pi ≥ 2. API: Construct the product of intervals and complex discs from positive radii; membership, compactness, convexity, symmetry and the volume formula. Tests: (1) all-real case attains the Minkowski volume threshold; (2) one complex place contributes pi times radius squared; (3) alpha=0 is rejected.

items.name: Small inverse-ideal multiplier
items.statement: Under the balanced-body hypotheses, there exists κ ∈ I^(-1), κ ≠ 0, with |κ|_v ≤ D_K^(1/(2n)) |α|_v^(-1/m) for every infinite place v.
items.note: Use compact non-strict Minkowski and the fractional-ideal covolume, retaining a nonzero witness.

items.name: Archimedean-balanced generator of a torsion representative
items.statement: For a degree-n number field K and an ideal class of exact order m ≥ 1, there exist a nonzero integral ideal J in the class and nonzero β ∈ O_K with J^m = (β) and |β|_v ≤ D_K^(m/(2n)) for every infinite place v.
items.note: Construct J = κI and β = ακ^m. The order-dividing variant is extracted separately in this continuation.

items.name: Balanced generator for an order-two class
items.statement: For a degree-n number field K and an ideal class of exact order two, there are a nonzero integral representative J and nonzero β ∈ O_K with J² = (β) and |β|_v ≤ D_K^(1/n) at every infinite place.
items.note: For all 2-torsion include the identity through balanced-order-dividing. Only |N(β)| = N(J)² is forced; the field norm can be negative.

items.name: Reduced integral basis starting with one
items.statement: For every degree-n number field with n≥2, there is a Z-basis 1,v_1,...,v_(n−1) of O_K, nondecreasing in the trace-weighted Euclidean norm, such that ||v_i||_tr≤(3/2)^i||w||_tr for every 1≤i≤n−1 and integral w outside span_Q(1,v_1,...,v_(i−1)). The product Π_(i=1)^(n−1)||v_i||_tr is bounded above and below by positive degree-dependent multiples of sqrt(D_K).
items.locator: BSTTTZ §3 p.5, originally citing Siegel Lecture X §6; replacement proof in the fourth-checkpoint supplement B1–B3
items.note: Original Siegel proof remains unread. The present route instead uses trace-metric-normalization, primitive-prefix-extension with u=1 and A=1, and reduced-basis-product. The comparison now includes i=n−1. Generic reduction belongs to GN.5, consuming GN.0/GN.1; the number-field specialization belongs to EffectiveBoundsClassGroupTorsion. API: a basis extending 1, primitive saturated prefixes, all-index length comparison, trace-metric ordering, degree-uniform product bounds and explicit comparison with ordinary Euclidean lengths. Tests: (1) the quadratic case has exactly one nonconstant vector; (2) the last-index comparison is present; (3) Q(i) uses trace covolume two while ordinary covolume is one. Sorting is asserted only in the trace metric, not simultaneously in both metrics. This integrates the earlier direct proof candidate, not an independent review or a Lean implementation.

items.name: Top-coordinate multiplication matrix
items.statement: For n ≥ 3 and a basis 1,v_1,...,v_(n-1), form the symmetric (n−2)-square rational matrix A whose entry a_ij is the coefficient of v_(n−1) in v_i v_j, for 1 ≤ i,j ≤ n−2.
items.note: This is a coordinate construction on field multiplication, not the trace Gram matrix. API: Use basis.repr of products and Matrix.det, with symmetry and invariance of the rational hyperplane under a kernel witness. Tests: (1) cubic basis produces a one-by-one matrix; (2) quadratic extension needs a separate empty-matrix argument; (3) trace Gram matrices have different entries.

items.name: Nondegeneracy of the top-coordinate multiplication matrix
items.statement: For any degree-n extension K/Q with n ≥ 3 and Q-basis 1,v_1,...,v_(n−1), the top-coordinate multiplication matrix has nonzero determinant.
items.note: A nonzero kernel vector r in span(v_1,...,v_(n−2)) makes multiplication by r preserve L = span(1,...,v_(n−2)). Since r is not rational, [Q(r):Q] ≥ 2 divides both n and n−1, a contradiction. The permutation term in the nonzero determinant still needs its own proof node at blueprint time.

items.name: Degree-dependent upper bound for the largest minimum
items.statement: For every n≥2 there is C_n>0 such that every degree-n number field K satisfies λ_n(O_K)≤C_n D_K^(1/n) for its ordinary archimedean Euclidean lattice. The trace-reduced basis constructed in reduced-integral-basis also satisfies ||v_i||_tr≤C_n D_K^(1/n) for every i.
items.note: For n=2 use the reduced-basis product bound. For n≥3, choose a nonzero permutation term of the top-coordinate multiplication matrix; its n−2 products lie outside the penultimate span. The last-index comparison and submultiplicativity of the trace norm give L^(n−2)≪Π_(i=1)^(n−2)||v_i||_tr², where L=||v_(n−1)||_tr. Multiplying by L² and using the product estimate gives L^n≪D_K. Trace ordering bounds the whole basis, and ||.||_0≤||.||_tr transfers the conclusion to ordinary successive minima. This uses the replacement B1–B3 argument, not an unread Siegel assertion; nonzero determinant-term extraction and exact generic library interfaces remain blueprint tasks.

items.name: Coarse count of small algebraic integers
items.statement: For fixed n and c > 0, the number of β ∈ O_K with |β|_v ≤ c D_K^(1/n) at every infinite place is O_(n,c)(D_K^(1/2)), uniformly over degree-n number fields K.
items.note: Use a uniformly controlled fundamental parallelepiped and disjoint-translate volumes, not a fixed-lattice asymptotic with field-dependent error.

items.name: Balanced generators for classes killed by m
items.statement: Let K be a degree-n number field, m ≥ 1 and c ∈ Cl(K) with c^m = 1. There exist a nonzero integral ideal J representing c and nonzero β ∈ O_K with J^m = (β) and |β|_v ≤ D_K^(m/(2n)) at every infinite place.
items.locator: Theorem 2.1 proof p.4, logical order-dividing extension used in §4
items.note: The proof uses only I^m principal, not exact order m. This extends rather than misquotes the displayed theorem; in particular it includes the identity class.

items.name: Injecting 2-torsion into balanced square-norm elements
items.statement: For K of degree n set R = D_K^(1/n) and B_K(R) = {β ∈ O_K : |β|_v ≤ R for every infinite v}. Choosing the order-dividing-m=2 representatives defines an injection Cl(K)[2] → {β ∈ B_K(R) : β ≠ 0 and |N_K/Q(β)| is an integer square}.
items.locator: Opening of §4 p.6; injectivity and norm-sign details expanded in this report
items.note: If two chosen generators agree, their ideal squares agree; unique factorization of nonzero ideals then identifies the ideals and their classes. Use both norm signs. API: Choose representatives via balanced-order-dividing; prove nonzeroness, square-norm membership, ideal-power cancellation and injectivity. Tests: (1) identity class is included; (2) negative signed norm is allowed; (3) equal generators force equal integral ideals.

items.name: A uniform variable-radius integer count
items.statement: For each d ≥ 1 there is C_d such that for every degree-d number field F and every real T ≥ D_F^(1/d), the number of α ∈ O_F with |α|_v ≤ T at every infinite place is at most C_d T^d / sqrt(D_F).
items.locator: §4 p.6, expansion of the subfield-box estimate following Lemma 4.1
items.note: From the controlled integral basis and largest-minimum theorem, a fundamental parallelepiped lies in a degree-dependent dilation of the T-box. Disjoint translates and covolume prove the bound. Treat F=Q directly.

items.name: The monic integral norm polynomial
items.statement: For β ∈ O_K define P_β(X) as the characteristic polynomial of multiplication by β on the free Z-module O_K. It is monic in Z[X], has degree [K:Q], and satisfies P_β(t) = N_K/Q(t−β) for t ∈ Q.
items.locator: §4 p.6 norm polynomial; monic sign convention expanded here
items.note: The paper uses N(β−X) = (−1)^n P_β(X). Import the existing characteristic-polynomial, determinant and norm APIs rather than creating duplicate carriers; the packaged comparison has not been matched to an exact pinned declaration. API: Reuse multiplication endomorphisms and characteristic polynomials; monicity, degree, scalar extension, evaluation as norm and translation. Tests: (1) rational beta has P=(X-beta)^n; (2) primitive beta has its minimal polynomial; (3) odd degree changes the sign of N(beta-X).

items.name: Multiplicity of the roots of a norm polynomial
items.statement: Let β ∈ O_K, let q_β ∈ Z[X] be its monic minimal polynomial, and set e = [K:Q(β)]. Then P_β = q_β^e, and every complex root of P_β has multiplicity e.
items.note: Use restriction of scalars from Q(β) or the norm tower, and separability in characteristic zero. The exponent uses the generated field Q(β), not an arbitrary subfield containing β.

items.name: Square norm polynomials and even generated-field index
items.statement: For β ∈ O_K, P_β is a square in C[X] if and only if [K:Q(β)] is even. In the even case its monic square root lies in Z[X].
items.locator: Lemma 4.1, §4 p.6, with the monic sign convention
items.note: Apply the root multiplicity statement. For the paper’s signed norm polynomial, being a square may require multiplication by −1.

items.name: Absolute irreducibility of the unreduced norm curve
items.statement: Let K have degree n ≥ 3 and β ∈ O_K with e = [K:Q(β)] odd. For each s ∈ {1,−1}, the affine plane curve Y² − sP_β(X) = 0 is absolutely irreducible of total degree n.
items.locator: §4 p.6, replacement of the squarefree-part step by an unreduced norm curve
items.note: P_β is not a square in C(X), so the monic quadratic in Y is irreducible there; Gauss’s lemma gives irreducibility in C[X,Y]. Repeated roots can make the curve singular, but do not change total degree or this conclusion. This is an explicit proof repair, not a verbatim named source lemma.

items.name: Counting the even-index exceptional locus
items.statement: Let K have fixed degree n ≥ 3 and no subfield F with [K:F] = 2. Among β ∈ O_K satisfying |β|_v ≤ D_K^(1/n) at every infinite place, the number with [K:Q(β)] even is O_n(D_K^(1/4)).
items.note: For F=Q(β) its even index e is at least 4. The discriminant tower gives D_F^(e) ≤ D_K, so variable-radius-box-count applies and yields O_n(D_K^(1/e)/sqrt(D_F)). Sum over the bounded number of subfields (for example at most 2^(n!)). In odd degree the exceptional locus is empty. The discriminant and subfield machinery must be imported from its baseline supplier.

items.name: Uniform count of integer-translation classes
items.statement: For a degree-n number field K with n ≥ 3, set R = D_K^(1/n). The number of additive cosets in O_K/Z meeting B_K(R) is O_n(D_K^(1/2−1/n)).
items.locator: Final paragraph of §4 p.6; boundary-safe proof expanded in this report
items.note: Choose one β_L in each nonempty coset. The pairs (L,m), |m| ≤ floor(R), inject by β_L+m into B_K(2R). Divide the coarse count for the enlarged box by 2 floor(R)+1. Do not assume every fiber inside the original box has length comparable to R.

items.name: Both norm signs in a bounded norm-curve rectangle
items.statement: For K of degree n ≥ 3, R = D_K^(1/n), β_0 ∈ B_K(R) and α = β_0−m ∈ B_K(R) with m ∈ Z, α ≠ 0 and |N(α)| = y² for y ∈ Z_≥0, one has |m| ≤ 2R and 0 < y ≤ sqrt(D_K). The assignment α ↦ (s,m,y), with s chosen so that y² = sP_β0(m), injects into the union of the two norm curves in this rectangle.
items.locator: §4 p.6, with the ± sign made explicit as in §5.1 p.7
items.note: The sign also incorporates P_β0(m) = (−1)^n N(α). The norm is nonzero. The rectangle fits an integer translate of a square of side at most C_n sqrt(D_K). API: Recover the translation integer, positive square root and sign; prove bounds, inverse recovery and the unchanged generated field. Tests: (1) negative norm selects the other curve; (2) zero alpha is excluded; (3) integer translation preserves generated-field index.

items.name: The square-norm saving on one translation class
items.statement: For every n ≥ 3 and ε > 0 there is C_(n,ε) such that, uniformly over degree-n fields K and β_0 ∈ B_K(D_K^(1/n)) with [K:Q(β_0)] odd, the number of nonzero α ∈ (β_0+Z) ∩ B_K(D_K^(1/n)) whose absolute norm is a square is at most C_(n,ε) D_K^(1/(2n)+ε).
items.locator: Final paragraph of §4 p.6, with the unreduced norm-curve repair
items.note: Apply the coefficient-uniform Bombieri–Pila theorem to each absolutely irreducible degree-n signed curve in a square of side O_n(sqrt(D_K)). Q(β_0+m)=Q(β_0). The proof permits singular curves; it does not give the lower-degree squarefree part the wrong degree n.

items.name: Square-norm count without an index-two subfield
items.statement: For every n ≥ 3 and ε > 0, uniformly over degree-n fields K having no subfield of index two, the number of nonzero β ∈ O_K with |β|_v ≤ D_K^(1/n) at all infinite places and |N(β)| an integer square is O_(n,ε)(D_K^(1/2−1/(2n)+ε)).
items.locator: §4 p.6, expanded combination of the odd- and even-index cases
items.note: Multiply the translation-coset count by the odd-index bound and add O_n(D_K^(1/4)) for the even-index locus. Since n ≥ 3, that error is absorbed. This proof consumes the recorded lattice lemmas and the original Bombieri–Pila input.

items.name: The general-exponent torsion bound in the no-index-two case
items.statement: For every n ≥ 3 and ε > 0 there is C_(n,ε) such that every degree-n number field K with no subfield F satisfying [K:F]=2 has |Cl(K)[2]| ≤ C_(n,ε) D_K^(1/2−1/(2n)+ε).
items.locator: Theorem 1.1 general exponent and §4 p.6, explicitly restricted to the branch whose proof is expanded here
items.note: Combine torsion-square-norm-injection with balanced-square-norm-count. This includes all odd degrees. The general even-degree completion now uses quadratic-relative-torsion and all-degree-torsion-induction, not the literal unverified relative-genus-source-claim. The sharper cubic and quartic exponents require their separate inputs.

items.name: Coefficient-uniform Bombieri–Pila plane-curve estimate
items.statement: Let C be an absolutely irreducible affine plane curve of total degree d ≥ 2, and let N ≥ exp(d^6). The number of integral points on C in [0,N] × [0,N] is at most N^(1/d) exp(12 sqrt(d log N log log N)).
items.locator: Bombieri–Pila, The number of integral points on arcs and ovals, Theorem 5, author preprint p.17; cited in BSTTTZ §4 p.6
items.note: The selected original proof path consists of the extracted determinant, auxiliary-curve and derivative-partition items. The sixth-checkpoint supplement BP1–BP6 adds the integer-parameter proof of constant 11 and an explicit 8d^3 cover of the integer points, including singular/boundary points; log(8d^3)≤sqrt(d log N loglog N) gives constant 12. This replacement does not assume smoothness of C or coefficient-height bounds. Proper Bézout, analytic branch continuation and exact generic supplier matching remain G7; no Lean implementation or independent review is claimed.

items.name: Translated-square epsilon form of Bombieri–Pila
items.statement: For each integer d ≥ 2 and real ε > 0 there is C_(d,ε) such that every absolutely irreducible real plane curve of total degree d has at most C_(d,ε) N^(1/d+ε) integer points in any integer translate of [0,N]², for every N ≥ 1. The constant is independent of the curve coefficients and the translating integers.
items.locator: Elementary consequence of Bombieri–Pila Theorem 5, author preprint p.17; form consumed in BSTTTZ §4
items.note: For large N absorb the subpower exponential; for the bounded remaining interval use the grid count (floor(N)+1)². Integer translation preserves integral points and total degree.

items.name: Ordinary class-group 2-torsion
items.statement: Cl(K)[2] is the kernel of c ↦ c² on the ordinary ideal class group; h₂(K) is its finite cardinality and r₂(K)=log₂ h₂(K).
items.note: API: Use the existing group kernel rather than a new class-group type; prove finiteness, F₂-vector-space structure and h₂=2^r₂. Tests: (1) the identity belongs to the kernel; (2) a cyclic group of order four has two elements killed by two; (3) an odd-order group has h₂=1.

items.name: Packing and feedback constants
items.statement: Put u=√3/2, b=((1+u)/(2u)) log((1+u)/(2u))−((1−u)/(2u)) log((1−u)/(2u)), a=1/(6(1−b/log 2)), c=ab/log 2. All logarithms except log₂ are natural.
items.note: API: Define exact real constants; prove positivity and b<log 2 before dividing; expose a=1/6+c. Tests: (1) b lies between .27823 and .27825; (2) a lies between .27843 and .27844; (3) c lies between .11176 and .11178.

items.name: Index-two reduction requiring an original-source check
items.statement: The author copy claims: if [K:F]=2, h₂(K) is bounded by h₂(F) times O(2^t), where t counts ramified primes of K/F, and consequently h₂(K)≪_{n,ε}D_K^(1/4+ε). This literal dependence on h₂(F) is NOT certified here.
items.note: G2: the literal one-factor h_2(F) claim and its advertised D_K^(1/4+epsilon) conclusion remain unverified, and this diagnostic item stays unrouted. The integrated Klüners–Wang replacement uses h_2(F)^2 and proves the general exponent by strong degree induction; it is not verification of this stronger displayed source assertion. Any future direct verification must retain ambiguous versus all 2-torsion classes, capitulation, unit, base-class and finite/infinite ramification terms.

items.name: Main class-group torsion bound in degrees above four
items.statement: For every n>4 and ε>0 there is C_(n,ε) such that h₂(K)≤C_(n,ε)D_K^(1/2−1/(2n)+ε) for every degree-n number field K.
items.note: Derive this source target from all-degree-torsion-induction. The replacement primitive-prefix proof and Klüners–Wang relative-rank argument are integrated as explicit missing nodes, importing GN.1/GN.5 and the upstream ordinary Hilbert class field. The literal Siegel/genus assertions are not used as unverified premises. Full paper closure, exact generic declaration audit and independent review are still pending.

items.name: Sharper cubic 2-torsion bound
items.statement: For every ε>0, h₂(K)≪_ε D_K^(a+ε) uniformly over cubic number fields K, with exact a from feedback-constants.
items.note: The cubic case has no index-two subfield. The replacement trace-reduced basis is now explicitly routed; the unacquired Brumer–Kramer original input and the remaining HV proof interiors are still G3.

items.name: Sharper quartic 2-torsion bound
items.statement: For every ε>0, h₂(K)≪_ε D_K^(a+ε) uniformly over quartic number fields K.
items.note: Requires the cubic resolvent comparison and all reducible cases, not only S₄ fields; see G4.

items.name: Solving the cubic feedback inequality
items.statement: Suppose for every η>0, H(D)≤C_η D^(1/6+η) exp((b+η)log₂ H(D)) for D≥1 and H(D)≥1, with b<log 2. Then for every ε>0, H(D)≪_ε D^(a+ε).
items.note: Choose η with θ=(b+η)/log 2<1; raise both sides to 1/(1−θ), and use continuity at η=0. Fixed positive epsilon cannot simply be removed.

items.name: Absorbing prime-support factors
items.statement: For fixed A≥1 and ε>0, A^ω(m)≪_(A,ε)m^ε for positive integers m, uniformly in m; ω counts distinct prime divisors.
items.note: Split primes at A^(1/ε): finitely many small primes contribute a fixed constant, each large-prime factor A is at most p^ε. Use this on model discriminants and retain fixed degree.

items.name: Restricted monomial system
items.statement: A finite nonempty set M of distinct monomials X^iY^j has D=|M|, p=Σ(i+j), q=Σj; evaluation at points gives a matrix with one column per monomial.
items.note: API: Reuse MvPolynomial and finite exponent sets; evaluation, cardinality and degree sums, nonzero coefficient vectors and curve kernels. Tests: (1) constant monomial contributes zero to p and q; (2) q≤p always; (3) duplicate monomials must not inflate D.

items.name: Scaled derivative bound
items.statement: For N>0, a compact interval I⊂[0,N] and f∈C^k(I), define ||f||_(N,k)=max_{0≤i≤k,x∈I} N^(i−1)|f^(i)(x)|/i!.
items.note: API: Prove finite maxima, dilation invariance, product bound and the estimates for X^i f^j. Tests: (1) dilation f_t(x)=tf(x/t) preserves the norm; (2) the zero function has norm zero; (3) the constant function has norm |c|/N.

items.name: Auxiliary curve from evaluation rank deficiency
items.statement: The selected points lie on the zero locus of a nonzero polynomial supported in M if and only if their monomial evaluation matrix has rank <D.
items.note: Consume ordinary matrix rank/kernel and polynomial monomial independence; do not create a second generic linear-algebra owner.

items.name: Vandermonde derivative bound
items.statement: For D distinct x_i in I and f_j∈C^(D−1)(I), |det(f_j(x_i))| ≤ |Vandermonde(x_i)| D! N^(−D(D−3)/2) ∏_j ||f_j||_(N,D−1).
items.note: Interpolation divided differences and repeated mean-value theorem; pointwise derivative witnesses can differ between matrix entries. Coincident abscissae instead make determinant zero.

items.name: Integer determinant forces separation
items.statement: A nonzero integer monomial evaluation determinant has absolute value at least one. Combining this with the derivative estimate bounds the abscissa span below by (D^p ||f||_(N,D−1)^q)^(−2/(D(D−1))) N^(1−2p/(D(D−1))), for D≥2.
items.note: Use a maximal nonvanishing minor in an ordered block; handle vanishing derivative-bound factor separately rather than dividing by zero.

items.name: Generalized determinant covering lemma
items.statement: For D≥2 and f∈C^(D−1)(I), all integral points on its graph lie on at most (D^p ||f||_(N,D−1)^q)^(2/(D(D−1))) N^(2p/(D(D−1)))+1 curves defined in M.
items.note: Count successive maximal blocks by disjoint spans; floor/ceiling convention must turn the real upper bound into an integer count.

items.name: Monomials avoiding the leading term
items.statement: For a degree-d plane polynomial F and integer δ≥2d, select monomials of degrees d through δ not divisible by the degree-d term of largest Y-degree in F. Then D=d(δ−d+1), p=d(δ(δ+1)−d(d−1))/2.
items.note: API: Define the degree-then-Y monomial order, avoidance predicate, counts, and show no nonzero supported polynomial is divisible by F. Tests: (1) exactly d monomials survive at each degree h≥d; (2) δ=2d satisfies D≥2; (3) a multiple of F has a forbidden leading term.

items.name: Auxiliary curves meet the original properly
items.statement: If F is absolutely irreducible of degree d and 0≠G is supported in its selected monomials through degree δ, then F∤G and their affine intersection has at most dδ geometric points.
items.note: Import SF.5 isolated/proper Bézout; cardinal upper bound, not equality, and the zero polynomial is excluded.

items.name: Uniform bound for derivative level sets
items.statement: For a nonpolynomial analytic branch g of an absolutely irreducible degree-b plane curve, the equation g^(k)(x)=c has at most b(b−1)(2k−1) solutions for k≥1.
items.note: Implicit differentiation gives denominator G_y^(2k−1); remove critical points first, and use proper intersection. Polynomial branches are handled separately.

items.name: Partition by derivative thresholds
items.statement: Given positive A_1,...,A_k, a smooth degree-b algebraic graph can be divided into at most 2b²k² intervals on each of which every |g^(i)| is entirely ≤A_i or entirely ≥A_i.
items.note: Include endpoints and the polynomial-branch alternative; avoid counting a derivative identically equal to a threshold as infinitely many cutting points.

items.name: Large derivative implies short interval
items.statement: Let k≥1 be an integer, A,N>0, a≤b, and g∈C^k([a,b]). If |g^(i)(x)|≤i! A^(i/k)N^(1−i) for 0≤i<k and |g^(k)(x)|≥k! A N^(1−k) throughout [a,b], then b−a≤2 A^(−1/k)N.
items.note: The sixth-checkpoint supplement BP2 gives the complete Taylor argument with t=(b−a)A^(1/k)/N. The identity t^k−Σ_(i=1)^(k−1)t^i−2=(t−2)Σ_(i=0)^(k−1)t^i gives t≤2, including k=1 and the degenerate interval. Source issue E1 records the printed opposite exponent. Exact Taylor supplier matching and Lean elaboration remain unclaimed.

items.name: Coefficient-uniform algebraic graph bound
items.statement: Let d≥2 be an integer, N≥exp(d^6), and f a C-infinity real function on a neighbourhood of a compact interval I⊂[0,N]. If |f′|≤1 on I and F(x,f(x))=0 for an absolutely irreducible real plane polynomial F of total degree d, its graph over I has at most N^(1/d)exp(11√(d log N loglog N)) integral points.
items.note: The sixth-checkpoint supplement BP1–BP5 supplies integer-only normalization, contraction stopping, the H+K inequalities and delta=floor(2 sqrt(log N/(d loglog N))). It proves the exact constant 11 conditional on the extracted determinant/partition inputs. Use q≤p, not the printed reverse inequality. G7 now concerns exact generic supplier matching and independent verification, not an unwritten integer-rounding argument. No Lean proof or independent acceptance is claimed.

items.name: Plane curve decomposes into bounded-slope arcs
items.statement: An absolutely irreducible degree-d plane curve in a square decomposes into O(d²) smooth graph pieces, each with slope at most one relative to one coordinate axis, together with O(d²) exceptional points.
items.note: The source claims a stronger O(d²) whole-curve decomposition, whose exact singular/end-point treatment is not verified by the sixth checkpoint. The new bp-explicit-graph-cover instead proves an 8d³ cover of the finite integer-point set and suffices for constant 12; it is not asserted to prove this stronger original item. Keep this original target for possible later refinement, not as a premise of the replacement route.

items.name: Explicit elliptic 2-Selmer group
items.statement: For an elliptic Weierstrass model in characteristic-not-two normal form over a number field, intersect the norm-square kernel in its cubic étale square-class algebra with the local Kummer images at every finite and infinite place.
items.note: API: Import selmerGroup₂, membership and the inclusion of the global Kummer image. The comparison with cohomological Sel₂ is a separate EC.7 theorem. Tests: (1) split cubic algebra retains all factors; (2) a norm-square class can fail a local condition; (3) global point images pass every local condition.

items.name: Finite generation of elliptic rational points
items.statement: For an elliptic Weierstrass curve over a number field K, E(K) is a finitely generated abelian group.

items.name: Cardinality bounds the Mordell–Weil rank
items.statement: For any finite subgroup S of the explicit square-class target containing the Kummer image, 2^rank E(K)·#E(K)[2]≤#S, assuming finite generation of E(K).
items.note: This actual pinned statement requires finiteness of S; it does not itself prove selmerGroup₂ finite.

items.name: Elliptic canonical height with the HV normalization
items.statement: Use ĥ(P)=lim_n h_x(2^nP)/(2·4^n), the height for the origin divisor. It differs from h_x(P)/2 by a model-dependent bounded quantity.
items.note: API: Import canonicalHeight, its proved convergence and quadraticity; keep the factor 1/2 when comparing with the EC roadmap text. Tests: (1) ĥ(0)=0; (2) ĥ(2P)=4ĥ(P); (3) the EC roadmap convention without 1/2 is twice this height.

items.name: Explicit and cohomological 2-Selmer comparison
items.statement: For E/K over a number field, identify its explicit étale-algebra 2-Selmer group with the cohomological group cut out by all local Kummer images.
items.note: Reviewed AUDIT-11: general Selmer/Kummer sequence is absent; finite square-class containers alone are insufficient.

items.name: Height/rank interpolation function
items.note: API: Prove continuous endpoint extension and attainment of the minimum; export β(0)=b, α(x)≤β(0) and α(x)≤x. Tests: (1) t=1 uses the zero-log-zero limit; (2) x=0 gives α=0; (3) t=0 gives the pure packing bound.

items.name: Height-sensitive S-integral point bound
items.statement: For E/K with an integral Weierstrass equation, S containing every infinite place and every prime dividing its discriminant, s=|S|, h₀≥1, 0≤t≤1 and ε>0 sufficiently small, the number of S-integral points with ĥ≤h₀ is ≪_(ε,[K:Q]) C^s ε^(−2(s+[K:Q])) s^[K:Q](1+log h₀)^2 exp(t[K:Q]h₀+(β(t)+ε)rank E(K)).
items.note: Statement and proof read. Inputs: local repulsion partitions, positive-height lower bound, spherical-code estimate and torsion bound; their full original proof closure remains G3.

items.name: Optimized height/rank bound
items.statement: With the same E,K,S and h₀, let R≥max(1,rank E(K)). Replace the exponential in hv-height-count by exp(Rα([K:Q]h₀/R)+εR), retaining its prefactors.
items.note: The printed E(Q) in the general-number-field rank hypothesis must be E(K), as follows from the preceding theorem. R≥1 avoids division by zero.

items.name: All integral points controlled by rank and discriminant
items.statement: For every ε>0 and an elliptic integral Weierstrass model over Q of nonzero discriminant Δ, #E(Z)≪_ε |Δ|^ε exp((b+ε)rank E(Q)).
items.note: Read Corollary 3.11 and proof: choose S=∞ plus all bad primes, include Z-points in S-points, and absorb C^s, logarithms and prime support into |Δ|^ε. The original corollary has explicit s and largest-prime factors; it is not a bound with constants independent of S before this step.

items.name: Selmer dimension through a cubic étale class group
items.statement: For E:y²=f(x) over Q, f a nonsingular integral monic cubic and A=Q[x]/f, dim_F₂ Sel₂(E)≤dim_F₂ Cl(A)[2]+2ω(|Δ_E|)+2, where Cl(A) is the product of the maximal-order class groups of its field factors.
items.locator: BSTTTZ Theorem 5.2 p.8, citing Brumer–Kramer Proposition 7.1
items.note: G3: source theorem as quoted by the main paper; original Proposition 7.1 and following remark still not acquired. Preserve the chosen integral model and all local bad-prime terms.

items.name: Elliptic curves from cubic norm polynomials
items.statement: The balanced translation cosets for a cubic field give O(D_K^(1/6)) signed equations ±y²=x³+Ax²+Bx+C with |A|≪D_K^(1/3), |B|≪D_K^(2/3), |C|≪D_K; counted points have |x|≪D_K^(1/3), |y|≪D_K^(1/2).
items.note: API: Construct signed models from the unreduced cubic norm polynomial, bound elementary symmetric coefficients and discriminants, and inject nontrivial torsion classes into smooth fibers. Tests: (1) rational beta gives a singular cubic and must be separated; (2) negative sign converts by X=-x with sign changes of A,C; (3) nonrational beta in a cubic field is primitive.

items.name: Rational balanced generators contribute only the identity class
items.statement: In a cubic number field, if a nonzero integral ideal J has J²=(a) for a rational algebraic integer a and |N(a)| is square, then a=±m² for a positive integer m and J=(m); its class is the identity.
items.locator: §5.1, explicit repair of the singular rational-generator case
items.note: |N(a)|=|a|³ implies |a| is square; equality of ideal squares cancels. This argument is about the selected generators, not all rational points on a singular cubic.

items.name: Discriminant of the cubic norm family
items.statement: For the smooth models in cubic-norm-family, 0<|Δ_E|≪D_K²; the cubic étale algebra is isomorphic to K, and D_K≤|disc(f)|=|Δ_E|/16 for a model y²=f with monic f.
items.note: Use the cubic discriminant polynomial and [O_K:Z[beta]]²D_K=|disc(f)|. Inequality is non-strict; changing to an isomorphic integral model needs an explicit coordinate map.

items.name: Cubic torsion feedback inequality
items.statement: For every η>0, h₂(K)≪_η D_K^(1/6+η) exp((b+η)log₂ h₂(K)) uniformly over cubic fields.
items.note: Combine the smooth norm family, all-integral HV bound, Brumer–Kramer and prime-support loss; absorb the identity separately and rescale eta after the discriminant bound.

items.name: Pointwise elliptic 2-Selmer bound
items.statement: For every ε>0, #Sel₂(E)≪_ε |Δ_E|^(a+ε), uniformly over elliptic curves given by integral nonsingular Weierstrass equations over Q.
items.note: For reducible cubic algebras use the product of factor class groups, quadratic genus bounds and D_A≤|disc(f)|. Complete the integral coordinate-change and cohomological comparison contracts.

items.name: Pointwise elliptic rank bound
items.statement: For every ε>0 there is C_ε with rank E(Q)≤C_ε+(a+ε)log₂|Δ_E| for every nonsingular integral Weierstrass model.
items.note: Take log₂ of the Selmer cardinal bound; this is an upper bound, never a computation of the actual rank.

items.name: Pointwise elliptic integral-point bound
items.statement: For every ε>0, #E(Z)≪_ε |Δ_E|^(c+ε) uniformly over integral nonsingular Weierstrass models, with c=ab/log 2.
items.note: Substitute the rank bound into HV and rescale epsilon. Integral points and Δ belong to the chosen model; rational isomorphisms do not preserve integral points automatically.

items.name: Hyperelliptic Selmer claim requiring local-condition repair
items.statement: Theorem 1.3(a) of the author copy claims a bound for #Sel₂(Jac(C)) using only the discriminant of A=Q[x]/f for C:y²=f(x), with f separable of degree n. The passage from this algebra discriminant to the local conditions of the curve model is unverified.
items.note: G5: do not export the printed bound until leading coefficient, even degree, twists, reducible A and primes dividing the polynomial-order index are checked. A fixed split algebra does not control the bad primes of all its curve models.

items.name: Hyperelliptic rank consequence requiring the same repair
items.statement: Theorem 1.3(b) asserts the associated logarithmic rank bound for Jac(C)(Q), using the same algebra-discriminant exponent as part (a). Its hypotheses and local terms must be reconciled with the published revision.
items.note: G5: separate main result, but not accepted or routed on the basis of the unsupported Selmer claim.

items.name: Degree-one del Pezzo point count requiring height comparison
items.statement: For a smooth degree-one del Pezzo surface over Q, the February author copy claims O_X(N^2.87) rational points of anticanonical height at most N, using its weighted sextic elliptic fibration.
items.note: G6: not routed. Need primitive weighted representatives, canonical-height comparison uniform in the varying integral fibers with the right leading constant, singular-fiber treatment and numerical optimization. This subsection is absent from arXiv v1.

items.name: Class group of a finite étale rational algebra
items.statement: For A=∏ K_i a finite étale Q-algebra, Cl(A)=∏Cl(O_(K_i)), h₂(A)=∏h₂(K_i), and D_A=∏|disc K_i|. These use maximal orders, not an arbitrary polynomial order.
items.note: API: Transport along algebra isomorphisms and factor permutations; expose product torsion and discriminant formulas. Tests: (1) Q³ has D=1 and h₂=1; (2) Q×a quadratic field reduces to its quadratic factor; (3) changing a polynomial order does not change A but may enlarge its discriminant.

items.name: Cubic étale resolvent of a quartic field
items.statement: For a quartic field K, let its Galois group act on the three partitions of the four embeddings into two unordered pairs. The associated degree-three finite étale Q-algebra is its cubic resolvent A.
items.note: API: Construct the three-element Galois set and its étale algebra; handle disconnected orbits, isomorphism invariance and comparison with resolvent orders. Tests: (1) S₄ acts transitively through S₃; (2) V₄ acts trivially and gives Q³; (3) a nontransitive action yields a product algebra rather than a cubic field.

items.name: Quartic-to-resolvent 2-torsion comparison
items.statement: For every ε>0, h₂(K)/h₂(A) is between C_ε^(-1)D_K^(-ε) and C_ε D_K^ε for quartic fields K and their cubic étale resolvent A.
items.locator: BSTTTZ Lemma 5.3 and Remark 5.4; Tsimerman Lemma 6.1
items.note: G4: Tsimerman §§5–6 read locally, but the adelic-torus proof interior and transfer from splitting-field discriminant to D_K remain to audit. Restricting the module identities to transitive subgroups treats reducible resolvents; a non-Galois quartic is not assumed S₄.

items.name: Maximal cubic resolvent discriminant comparison
items.statement: For the cubic étale resolvent A of a quartic field K, D_A≤D_K.
items.note: G4: requires the discriminant-preserving cubic resolvent order and passage to its maximal order, or an equally precise ramification proof. Original theorem not yet read; do not replace this by an equality of maximal-order discriminants.

items.name: Common nontrivial factor of the permutation modules
items.statement: Let M=F₂^4 with S₄ permuting its basis, M₀ the line spanned by the sum, M₁=M/M₀ and M₂ the image of the even-weight subspace in M₁. Let N=F₂^3 on the three pair partitions and N₀ its sum line. Then M₁/M₂ is trivial and N/N₀≅M₂ equivariantly.
items.note: API: Use quotient F₂-representations, the incidence of a pair partition and a weight-two vector modulo complements, and restriction to subgroups. Tests: (1) dimensions M₀,M₂,M₁/M₂ are 1,2,1; (2) N/N₀ has dimension two; (3) the isomorphism remains equivariant after restriction to V₄.

items.name: Discriminant-negligible comparison
items.statement: For bounded degree n of a Galois splitting field L and bounded torus dimension d, a positive quantity F is negligible if for every ε>0, D_L^(-ε)≪_(n,d,ε) F≪_(n,d,ε)D_L^ε.
items.note: API: Track both bounds, multiplication, inversion and changing ε; retain the discriminant of the actual splitting field. Tests: (1) a positive bounded constant is negligible; (2) D_L^c for fixed c>0 is not negligible; (3) one-sided upper bounds alone are insufficient.

items.name: Exact-sequence transfer input needing an owner and proof audit
items.statement: Tsimerman Theorem 5.1 states that an exact sequence of Q-tori split by a degree-bounded field has a class-group sequence whose homology cardinalities are discriminant negligible. Corollary 5.2 assigns a class quantity to finite Galois modules, Lemma 5.3 bounds it along exact sequences, and Corollary 5.4 makes trivial modules negligible.
items.note: G4 acquisition node, not a closed atomic extraction: split these four results and the torus class-group carrier after reading the full adelic/class-formation supplier and the Shyr/Brauer–Siegel proof. Do not route a duplicate torus library from this application.

items.name: Discriminant-ordered field counts
items.statement: For transitive G≤S_n and X>0, N_n(G,X) counts Q-isomorphism classes of degree-n fields with normal-closure permutation group G and absolute discriminant <X. A fixed quadratic resolvent F gives the subcount N_n(G,F,X).
items.note: API: Import ST.0 field-family and height-count conventions; prove finiteness, monotonicity and group/resolvent predicates. Tests: (1) normal-closure group is not Aut(K/Q); (2) strict versus non-strict discriminant cutoffs are explicit; (3) fixed F is additional data, not a uniformity assertion.

items.name: Weighted quartic-to-cubic counting estimate
items.statement: For a family F₃ of cyclic or noncyclic cubic fields and the A₄/S₄ quartic family F₄ whose resolvents lie in F₃, N(F₄,X)≪Σ_(K∈F₃,D_K<X) h₂(K)(log D_K)² (X/D_K)^(1/2).
items.note: G8: the main paper extends the original estimates to subfamilies; acquire Baily before asserting the exact family uniformity or multiplicities.

items.name: Cyclic cubic discriminant asymptotic
items.statement: N₃(C₃,X)~C₁ X^(1/2) for a positive constant C₁.
items.note: Only an O(X^(1/2)) input is consumed. Original Cohn argument not acquired; ST.3 owns selected field-count asymptotics.

items.name: Cubic count with fixed quadratic resolvent
items.statement: For each fixed quadratic field F, N₃(S₃,F,X)~C_F X^(1/2), with a positive constant depending on F.
items.locator: §6 equation (10), Bhargava–Shnidman Theorem 7 and Cohen–Morra Theorem 1.1(2), Corollary 7.6
items.note: G8: original references remain to read. Neither a bound for C_F nor pointwise convergence gives a uniform error term in F.

items.name: Converting the weighted cubic sum
items.statement: If a cubic family has counting function O_F(T^(1/2)) and h₂(K)≪_ηD_K^(a+η), then Σ_(D_K<X)h₂(K)(log D_K)²(X/D_K)^(1/2)≪_(F,ε)X^(1/2+a+ε) for every ε>0.
items.note: Dyadic shells suffice: each shell T contributes O(X^(1/2)T^(a+η)(log T)²); a>0 makes the shell sum dominated by its top end. Absorb logarithms after choosing η<ε.

items.name: A₄ quartic field bound
items.statement: For every ε>0, N₄(A₄,X)≪_ε X^(1/2+a+ε).
items.note: Combine Baily, Cohn and weighted-partial-summation. This counts fields, not quartic rings or polynomial presentations.

items.name: S₄ quartic bound with fixed quadratic resolvent
items.statement: For every fixed quadratic field F and every ε>0, N₄(S₄,F,X)≪_(F,ε)X^(1/2+a+ε).
items.note: Retain dependence on F in the final result; the source explicitly disclaims uniformity despite its estimate of C_F.

items.name: Function-field divisors and degree
items.statement: For a one-variable function field L/k, divisors are finite integer sums of normalized places, with degree Σ_P n_P[k(P):k].
items.note: API: Import TauCeti.Divisor, degree and principal divisors; use the existing coefficient order and degree homomorphism. Tests: (1) a degree-two closed point has degree two; (2) a nonzero constant has principal divisor zero; (3) degree is additive and weights residue degrees.

items.name: Degree-zero divisor class group
items.statement: For a function field L/k, Cl⁰(L/k) is the kernel of the existing degree map on divisor classes; the principal subgroup identifies linearly equivalent divisors.
items.note: API: Use degreeClass and its kernel; expose quotient surjectivity, representative degree and principal witness recovery. Tests: (1) principal divisors represent zero; (2) positive-degree divisors do not lie in Cl⁰; (3) finite-chart ideal class groups are not identified without an infinity comparison.

items.name: Finiteness of the degree-zero class group
items.statement: If k is finite and L/k is a function field, Cl⁰(L/k) is finite.
items.note: No exact-constants hypothesis is needed for this library finiteness theorem; exact constants are required elsewhere in the source application.

items.name: Riemann–Roch space and its dimension
items.statement: L(D)={0}∪{f∈L×:div(f)+D≥0}, a finite-dimensional k-subspace; ℓ(D)=dim_k L(D).
items.note: API: Import riemannRochSpace and Divisor.dim; nonzero membership via ord inequalities, monotonicity and finite-dimensionality. Tests: (1) zero belongs for every D; (2) L(0)=k requires exact constants; (3) negative-degree divisors have no nonzero sections.

items.name: Effective representative from Riemann’s inequality
items.statement: For a function field and a divisor D, ℓ(D)≥deg(D)+1−g. In particular a divisor of degree g has a nonzero section and is linearly equivalent to an effective divisor.
items.note: The second declaration moves a degree-zero D by nB with g≤n deg B; use n=1, B=E of degree g in this application. It does not construct E.

items.name: High-degree Riemann–Roch
items.statement: For a function field with exact constants k and deg D≥2g−1, ℓ(D)=deg D+1−g, with subtraction in Z.

items.name: Finite projective-space cardinality
items.statement: For a finite field k of q elements and a d-dimensional k-vector space V, #P(V)=Σ_(i=0)^(d−1)q^i=(q^d−1)/(q−1).
items.note: Actual Mathlib declarations read; quotient by all nonzero scalars, not squares. The formula handles d=0 as zero.

items.name: Existence of a degree-one divisor over finite constants
items.statement: A smooth projective geometrically integral curve over a finite field has a rational divisor of degree one, hence a divisor E of degree g. No rational point or effective degree-one divisor is asserted.
items.note: AUDIT-01 says this F. K. Schmidt target is still absent. It is already a named consequence in upstream AlgebraicCurves Layer 5; do not re-plan it. A Lang/Picard route must also discharge the Brauer obstruction.

items.name: Rational Picard classes over a finite field
items.statement: For a smooth projective geometrically integral curve over a finite field k, degree-zero rational divisor classes identify with Pic⁰_(C/k)(k), since the obstruction lies in Br(k)=0.
items.note: Upstream Layer D explicitly owns the functor/sheaf versus actual line-bundle obstruction. Rational divisor classes must not be inferred from a nonexistent chosen k-point.

items.name: Nonzero sections with even divisor
items.statement: Fix a divisor E of degree g on C/k. Let V=L(2E), and S_E={f∈V:f≠0 and every coefficient of div(f) is even}. This is a k×-stable subset of V minus zero, not asserted to be a subspace.
items.note: API: Define the coefficientwise evenness predicate on existing principal divisors, prove scalar invariance and inclusion into the projectivization. Tests: (1) a section with an odd zero is excluded; (2) multiplication by a nonsquare constant still preserves membership; (3) zero is excluded even though the valuation API has junk values there.

items.name: Projective sections map to 2-torsion
items.statement: For f∈S_E, divide the coefficients of div(f) by two to obtain an integral degree-zero divisor A_f. The class [A_f] depends only on the projective class of f and satisfies 2[A_f]=0.
items.note: API: Prove exact coefficient halving, degree zero using 2deg A=0, independence under scalar multiplication and codomain membership. Tests: (1) non-even coefficients cannot be rounded; (2) constant sections map to the identity; (3) global squares give principal half-divisors but even divisors need not come from squares.

items.name: Every 2-torsion class comes from an even-divisor section
items.statement: The map P(S_E)→Cl⁰(C)[2] in half-divisor-map is surjective.
items.note: For c=[D], deg D=0, use RR on E−D to choose D₊≥0 with D₊~E−D. Since 2D is principal, choose f with div(f)=2D₊−2E. Then f∈L(2E) and [half div f]=−c=c. Different D₊ may give different projective f; uniqueness is only for a fixed principal divisor.

items.name: Dimension of the section space used in the torsion count
items.statement: If deg E=g, then ℓ(2E)=g+1 over the exact finite constant field, including g=0.
items.note: deg(2E)=2g≥2g−1 invokes the imported high-degree theorem, without an effective E or a chosen rational point.

items.name: Finite-field Picard 2-torsion bound
items.statement: For a smooth projective geometrically integral genus-g curve C over a finite field k of q elements, #Pic⁰(C)(k)[2]≤(q^(g+1)−1)/(q−1).
items.note: Chain: degree-one divisor and Picard comparison suppliers; even-divisor projective surjection; dimension g+1; existing projective cardinality. No gonality or characteristic restriction. Existence/comparison are planned imports, not assumed formalized.

items.name: Gonality over the stated constant field
items.statement: The k-gonality of C is the minimum degree of a nonconstant k-morphism C→P¹. The second assertion only assumes existence of a degree-n map, not minimality.
items.note: API: Import finite morphisms and function-field degrees; record separable/inseparable degree and base-field dependence, and prove a chosen map bounds gonality. Tests: (1) P¹ has gonality one; (2) a degree-n map need not compute the minimum; (3) extension of the constant field may lower gonality.

items.name: Gonality-sensitive torsion claim awaiting an exact counting input
items.statement: The author copy asserts #Pic⁰(C)(k)[2]≪_n q^((1−1/n)g) whenever C admits a degree-n map to P¹ over k.
items.note: G9: no route. Sedunova Theorem 1 has an epsilon loss and its printed coefficient/q uniformity needs repair. The source gives only a one-sentence analogy; characteristic two and inseparable maps cannot be replaced by characteristic-zero norm-square curves.

items.name: Function-field determinant estimate and its uniformity gap
items.statement: Sedunova Theorem 1 prints #C(I²)≪_(d,ε)|I|^(1/d+ε), for an irreducible degree-d curve over F_q[T] and I the polynomials of degree at most m. Here |I|=q^(m+1).
items.note: G9: record the literal source, not a certified q-uniform theorem. For Y²=X and m=2 there are q² pairs, exceeding q^(3/2+3ε) with q-independent constant as q→∞ for ε<1/6. This also has a degree/length off-by-one issue later in the source. Bad-reduction primes and the height cost of coordinate changes require explicit treatment. No route until the correct usable statement is established.

items.name: Geometric 2-torsion outside characteristic two
items.statement: For a genus-g Jacobian over an algebraically closed field of characteristic different from two, the group of geometric 2-torsion points has cardinality 2^(2g); rational 2-torsion injects into it.
items.note: Reuse the abelian-variety multiplication/isogeny supplier; distinguish point cardinality from finite group-scheme rank. Import and refine the existing Layer-E multiplication/isogeny and characteristic-p torsion contract; AUDIT-01 confirms this general abelian-variety result is not implemented.

items.name: Geometric 2-torsion in characteristic two
items.statement: For a genus-g Jacobian in characteristic two, the geometric 2-torsion point group has cardinality 2^f, where f is its p-rank and 0≤f≤g. Thus its cardinality is at most 2^g; equality requires ordinarity.
items.locator: Remark 7.3, correction of the unqualified 2^g equality
items.note: The group scheme still has rank 2^(2g). The main theorem’s proof with even principal divisors remains characteristic-free and does not rely on a Kummer étale sequence. Import and refine the existing Layer-E multiplication/isogeny and characteristic-p torsion contract; AUDIT-01 confirms this general abelian-variety result is not implemented.

items.name: Transitivity and generated-field norm formula
items.statement: Norms in a finite free scalar tower compose; in a finite field extension L/K, N_(L/K)(x)=N_(K(x)/K)(x)^[L:K(x)].
items.note: Actual pinned statements read in Norm/Transitivity. This imports generic norm machinery; packaging an integral characteristic polynomial with multiplicities remains the norm-polynomial items.

items.name: Trace-weighted Euclidean metric on the mixed embedding
items.statement: For a number field K of signature (r,s) and degree n=r+2s, put ||x||_tr²=Σ_real |x_v|²+2Σ_complex |x_v|² on its existing mixed space. The diagonal real map scaling both real coordinates of each complex factor by sqrt(2) identifies this metric with ordinary Euclidean space and has determinant 2^s. Thus ||x||_0≤||x||_tr≤sqrt(2)||x||_0, and the integer lattice has covolume sqrt(D_K) for the metric-induced Euclidean volume. The vector 1 is primitive and shortest, of trace length sqrt(n).
items.locator: Fourth-checkpoint supplement in the companion report, B1; BSTTTZ §3 p.5 motivates the normalization
items.note: Replacement construction, not a new mixed-embedding carrier. The unchanged ordinary product measure still gives covolume 2^(-s)sqrt(D_K), by the actual pinned declaration integer-covolume. For nonzero integral alpha, AM–GM on all n conjugates and |N(alpha)|≥1 proves the shortest-vector assertion; O_K∩Q=Z proves primitivity. Owner: EffectiveBoundsClassGroupTorsion. API: traceNorm_sq, traceNorm_eq_norm_scaled, norm_le_traceNorm, traceNorm_le_sqrtTwo_mul_norm, traceCovolume_integerLattice, traceNorm_one, sqrt_degree_le_traceNorm_of_integral_ne_zero, and primitive_one. These are planning names, not existing Lean declarations. Tests: (1) Q has length and covolume one; (2) Q(i) has trace basis lengths sqrt(2) and trace covolume two, but ordinary covolume one; (3) a mixed signature scales both real coordinates of each complex factor and satisfies both norm comparisons.

items.name: A reduced basis extending a prescribed primitive short vector
items.statement: Let Λ be a full lattice in a real Euclidean space of dimension n≥1. Let A≥1 and let u be primitive in Λ with ||u||≤Aλ_1. There exists a Z-basis b_0=u,...,b_(n−1) such that for every 0≤i<n and w∈Λ outside span_Q(b_0,...,b_(i−1)), ||b_i||≤c_i||w||, where c_0=A and c_i=1+(1/2)Σ_(j<i)c_j for i≥1. If A=1, c_i=(3/2)^i and the whole basis is nondecreasing in length. For general A only the suffix from b_1 is asserted nondecreasing.
items.locator: Fourth-checkpoint supplement in the companion report, B2; direct replacement proof for the reduction input in BSTTTZ §3 p.5
items.note: Maintain a saturated prefix L_i, so Λ/L_i is free. Choose a shortest lift with primitive nonzero quotient image; existence follows by minimizing among the finitely many candidates no longer than one chosen candidate. For w outside the prefix, divide its quotient image by its positive content d, lift, and round the prefix coefficients to [-1/2,1/2]. This gives u′=w/d+Σt_jb_j and the displayed recurrence. Saturation at full rank proves that the result is a basis, not just an independent set. Later basis vectors are primitive-extension candidates at earlier stages, giving the stated ordering. Import generic free-module, primitive-submodule and finite bounded-lattice-point APIs; own the reduction theorem once in GeometryOfNumbersAndQuadraticArithmetic:GN.5. Acceptance tests: rank one and A=1; rejection of nonprimitive u=2 in Z; comparison at i=n−1; c_i=((A+2)/2)(3/2)^(i−1) for i≥1. This is an existence theorem, not a claimed implemented LLL algorithm.

items.name: Covolume comparison for the primitive-prefix reduced basis
items.statement: For the rank-n lattice and basis constructed in primitive-prefix-extension, let v_n>0 be the Euclidean volume of the unit ball. Then ||b_i||≤c_iλ_(i+1) for every 0≤i<n and covol(Λ)≤Π_i||b_i||≤(Π_i c_i)(2^n/v_n)covol(Λ).
items.locator: Fourth-checkpoint supplement in the companion report, B3
items.note: Among i+1 independent vectors attaining λ_(i+1), at least one is outside the i-dimensional preceding span, so primitive-prefix-extension applies. Hadamard gives the lower product bound; the existing planned GN.1 second-Minkowski theorem gives the upper bound. Import attainment and basis/covolume identification through GN.0/GN.1 rather than privately redeveloping them. Owner: GN.5. Acceptance tests: rank-one lattice aZ, n positive and Λ full-rank, and a short independent set of nonunit index which must not be called a Z-basis.

items.name: Ordinary Hilbert class fields and their characteristic quotients
items.statement: For a number field E, the ordinary Hilbert class field identifies finite abelian extensions unramified at all finite places and split at every real place with quotients of the ordinary class group Cl(E), compatibly with conjugation and restriction to quotient extensions. In particular Cl(E)/2Cl(E) corresponds to the maximal everywhere-unramified elementary abelian 2-extension of E.
items.locator: Upstream ClassFieldTheory Layers 11–13, especially Layer 13; Fourth-checkpoint supplement in the companion report, C1–C2
items.note: Planned import, not an implemented declaration. The actual upstream contract defines hilbertClassField from rayClassField at Modulus.one and plans gal_hilbertClassField_equiv_classGroup, maximal-unramified properties and splitting criteria. Use its global uniqueness/conjugation interfaces to show stability of the elementary-2 quotient when E/F is Galois. The narrow class field permits real ramification and is not a substitute. Do not create another class-field-theory roadmap or claim this named planned isomorphism is in the pinned Lean library.

items.name: The class-field extension cut out by quadratic coinvariants
items.statement: For a quadratic extension E/F, let A=Cl(E)/2Cl(E), let σ be the induced involution, and put T=σ−1, V=A/TA and s=dim_F2 V. Then T²=0 and dim_F2 A≤2s. In the elementary-2 ordinary Hilbert class field H/E corresponding to A, the fixed field M=H^(TA) is Galois over F and yields a central exact sequence 1→V→G=Gal(M/F)→C2→1. The group G is abelian, has order 2^(s+1), and |2G|≤2; the sequence is not asserted to split without a ramified place.
items.locator: Fourth-checkpoint supplement in the companion report, C1; Klüners–Wang arXiv:2003.12161v2, Theorem 2.1 proof, pp.3–4, with the quotient carrier made explicit
items.note: Use the quotient A, not an equivariant identification with Cl(E)[2] inferred from equal cardinalities. Rank-nullity and im T⊆ker T give dim A≤2s. The characteristic class-group quotient and conjugation compatibility make H/F Galois; stability of TA gives M/F. Trivial conjugation on V makes G abelian because G/V is cyclic. G is generated by V and a lift τ, so 2G is generated by 2τ and has at most two elements. Owner: EffectiveBoundsClassGroupTorsion, importing hilbert-class-field-input. API: inducedClassQuotientInvolution, T_sq_zero, stable_range_T, fixedField_range_T, restriction_exact, commutative_G, card_G and card_twoG_le_two, all planning names. Tests: (1) on Z/4×Z/2, σ(x,y)=(x,y+x mod 2) fixes all 2-torsion but not the quotient modulo two; (2) the unramified branch admits nonsplit C4; (3) a ramified place provides an actual order-two inertia lift, not just an arbitrary lift.

items.name: Relative 2-rank bound for a quadratic extension
items.statement: For every quadratic extension E/F of number fields, let t count the ramified places of F, including real places that become complex, and put e=max(t,1). With r_2(L)=dim_F2(Cl(L)/2Cl(L)), one has r_2(E)≤2(r_2(F)+e−1), hence h_2(E)≤4^(e−1)h_2(F)^2.
items.locator: Klüners–Wang arXiv:2003.12161v2, Theorem 2.1 and proof, pp.3–4; Fourth-checkpoint supplement in the companion report, C2
items.note: Apply quadratic-coinvariant-extension. If t>0, one order-two inertia lift splits G, so it is elementary abelian of rank s+1. Kill the at most t inertia generators; the quotient corresponds to an everywhere-unramified abelian extension of F and is a quotient of Cl(F), giving s+1−t≤r_2(F). If t=0, G itself is a quotient of Cl(F), and |2G|≤2 gives s≤dim(G/2G)≤r_2(F). Combine with r_2(E)≤2s. Preserve both branches and infinite inertia. This later auxiliary theorem replaces, but does not verify, the original one-factor relative-genus-source-claim. Owner: EffectiveBoundsClassGroupTorsion. Tests: t=0 permits a C4 extension; t=1 gives r_2(E)≤2r_2(F); finite and real ramification are both counted.

items.name: Ramified places bounded by relative-discriminant support
items.statement: For a quadratic extension E/F with [F:Q]=m≥1 and relative discriminant ideal Δ_(E/F), the number t of finite and infinite ramified places of F satisfies t≤mω(N_F/Q Δ_(E/F))+m≤mω(D_E)+m. Here D_E=D_F² N_F/Q Δ_(E/F), and ω counts distinct rational prime divisors of a positive integer.
items.locator: Fourth-checkpoint supplement in the companion report, C3
items.note: Each finite ramified prime divides the relative discriminant, at most m primes of F lie above a rational prime, and at most m real places ramify. Import the actual ramification/discriminant-tower and prime-fiber bounds from their existing suppliers; exact generic declaration matching remains a blueprint obligation. Relative ideal discriminant, its positive rational norm, and the absolute field discriminant are separate quantities. Owner: EffectiveBoundsClassGroupTorsion. Tests: relative discriminant norm one leaves only the infinite contribution; several prime ideals above one rational prime require the m factor; real-to-complex ramification is not silently dropped.

items.name: Uniform quadratic relative torsion bound with squared base factor
items.statement: For every m≥1 and η>0 there is C_(m,η)>0 such that every quadratic extension E/F with [F:Q]=m satisfies h_2(E)≤C_(m,η)D_E^η h_2(F)^2. The constant is uniform as the base field F varies. In particular h_2(Q)=1 gives h_2(E)≪_η D_E^η for quadratic fields E/Q.
items.locator: Fourth-checkpoint supplement in the companion report, C3–C4, deduced from Klüners–Wang Theorem 2.1
items.note: Exponentiate quadratic-relative-rank, use ramified-place-support, and absorb (4^m)^ω(D_E) with prime-support-loss; the infinite-place factor is degree-bounded. State h_2(Q)=1 separately through the existing class-group/PID supplier at blueprint time. This proof needs h_2(F)^2, not the unverified h_2(F) factor in the 2017 source. Owner: EffectiveBoundsClassGroupTorsion. Tests: varying F at fixed m must not enter the implied constant; quadratic fields give the D^η base case; the ramification-free branch still retains the squared class-group factor.

items.name: The general-exponent torsion bound by induction on absolute degree
items.statement: For every n≥3 and ε>0 there is C_(n,ε)>0 such that every degree-n number field K has h_2(K)≤C_(n,ε)D_K^(1/2−1/(2n)+ε). This follows from two-torsion-no-index-two and quadratic-relative-torsion, with the quadratic D^η base case. A quartic field containing a quadratic subfield satisfies the stronger h_2(K)≪_ε D_K^ε.
items.locator: Fourth-checkpoint supplement in the companion report, C4; replacement completion of the general-exponent route in BSTTTZ §4
items.note: Strong induction on n, not an assumption that every field has a quadratic tower to Q. With α_d=1/2−1/(2d), an index-two subfield F of degree m=n/2≥2 gives h_2(K)≪D_K^η D_F^(2α_m+2η)≤D_K^(α_m+2η), since D_F²≤D_K. The gain α_n−α_m=1/(2n)>0 and η=ε/4 suffice. For m=1 use the quadratic base case; for quartics with a quadratic subfield apply that base estimate with a suitably smaller η to both factors. This does not establish the sharper cubic exponent or the remaining quartic resolvent branch. Owner: EffectiveBoundsClassGroupTorsion. Tests: degree three has no index-two branch; degree four uses m=2; no quadratic subfield means the norm-curve branch, not a nonexistent induction step.

items.name: Integer-preserving normalization of a bounded-slope graph
items.statement: Let N≥1 and let g be C-infinity near a compact interval I of length at most N, with |g′|≤1. If its graph has at least two integral points, restrict I to the interval between their least and greatest integer abscissae. Integer translations of the two coordinates then put the new interval inside [0,N] and the graph inside [0,N]×[−N,N], preserving every counted integral point, total degree and absolute irreducibility of a defining polynomial.
items.locator: BP1 of the sixth-checkpoint supplement; expands Bombieri–Pila Theorem 4 proof, author preprint pp.15–16.
items.note: Choose the vertical integer nearest the midpoint of the range; the new absolute value is ≤N/2+1/2≤N. Zero/one-point cases are separate. No arbitrary real translation of the lattice is allowed. For 0<N<1 use at most one integer abscissa instead. This is a lemma about the existing real interval and polynomial carriers, not a new definition. Tests: noninteger original interval endpoints; graph y=x+M for large integer M; N=1 and the zero/one-point branches. Owner: IntegralPointDeterminantMethods.

items.name: Stopping a determinant recurrence below lattice scale
items.statement: Let G:(0,∞)→[0,∞), α>0, H≥0, K≥1 and 0<λ<1 with Kλ^α=1/2. Suppose G(x)≤Hx^α+KG(λx) for x≥1 and G(x)≤1 for 0<x<1. Then G(N)≤(2H+K)N^α≤2(H+K)N^α for every N≥1.
items.locator: BP3 of the sixth-checkpoint supplement; Bombieri–Pila Theorem 4 recurrence, author preprint pp.16–17.
items.note: For the least m with λ^mN<1, iterate m times. The residual term K^m equals 2^(−m)λ^(−mα) and is ≤2^(1−m)KN^α≤KN^α because λ^mN≥λ. The geometric sum is ≤2. Tests: N=1; λ^(m−1)N=1 with strict termination only at the next step; H=0. This numerical recurrence uses existing real powers and finite sums; no new generic owner.

items.name: Uniform determinant recurrence constants
items.statement: Let integers d≥2 and δ≥2d satisfy D=d(δ−d+1), p=d(δ(δ+1)−d(d−1))/2 and 0≤q≤p. Put α=2p/(D(D−1)), K=2d^4δ², λ=(2K)^(−1/α), A=(2/λ)^(D−1), X=(D^p A^q)^(2/(D(D−1))) and H=4d^5δ³X. Then Kλ^α=1/2 and H+K≤δ^(9dδ)/2. Consequently a graph-count function satisfying the preceding recurrence obeys G(N)≤N^(1/d)exp(4 log(N)/δ+9dδ log δ) for N≥1.
items.locator: BP4 of the sixth-checkpoint supplement; Bombieri–Pila Theorem 4 proof, author preprint pp.16–17.
items.note: Use 1/d≤α≤1/d+4/δ≤2, D≤dδ and X≤(DA)^α. The full inequality chain is in BP4, not a numerical approximation. Choose the worst case q=p when taking a maximum over polynomials, so H is uniform in their leading monomials. Derivative partitions give at most K intervals; the small-norm contribution is ≤HN^α and the remaining pieces have length ≤λN. Source issue E2 corrects the printed p≤q. Tests: d=2, δ=4; every possible leading Y-degree; the q=0 and q=p endpoints.

items.name: Integer parameter giving the Bombieri–Pila constant eleven
items.statement: For an integer d≥2 and N≥exp(d^6), put L=log N, ell=log L, S=sqrt(d L ell), x=2 sqrt(L/(d ell)) and δ=floor x. Then δ≥2d and 4L/δ+9dδ log δ≤11S.
items.locator: BP5 of the sixth-checkpoint supplement; repairs the unstated integer rounding in Bombieri–Pila Theorem 4, author preprint p.17.
items.note: The proof is analytic, not inferred from testing: δ≥3x/4 and δ≥L^(1/4); E(t)=4L/t+9dt log t has E′(t)≥(17/36)d ell+9d>0 on [δ,x]. Thus E(δ)≤E(x)=S[11+(9/ell)log(4/(d ell))]≤11S. BP5 proves all threshold inequalities, using log d≤d/2. Source issue E3 records the gap, not a false theorem. Tests: d=2 and log N=64; both sides of integer jumps of x; large d at the threshold.

items.name: A singularity-safe cover for the integral-point theorem
items.statement: For N>0 and an absolutely irreducible real plane polynomial F of total degree d≥2, its integral zeros in [0,N]² are covered by at most 8d³ sets, each either a singleton or contained in a C-infinity graph on a compact subinterval of [0,N] with absolute slope at most one relative to one coordinate axis. Each graph satisfies F, or F with coordinates exchanged. For N≥exp(d^6), the constant-eleven graph bound therefore implies the constant-twelve plane-curve bound.
items.locator: BP6 of the sixth-checkpoint supplement; replacement for the abbreviated final passage of Bombieri–Pila Theorem 5, author preprint p.17.
items.note: Use proper Bézout on F_Y, F_X+F_Y and F_X−F_Y, and horizontal boundary intersections. There are at most Q=3d(d−1)+2d critical abscissae. Each open strip has at most d simple analytic root graphs; invert steep ones, and restrict each to the compact hull of its finitely many integer points. Critical vertical fibers contribute at most d points each. The total is ≤d(Q+1)+d(Q+2)≤8d³; log(8d³)≤sqrt(d log N loglog N) absorbs it. No smoothness at the original singular endpoints is assumed. Generic proper-intersection/Bézout stays with SF.5; exact root-continuation and analytic inverse-function supplier matching remains G7. This does not prove the stronger O(d²) whole-curve claim. Tests: singular cusp Y²=X³; steep graphs needing axis exchange; integral points on critical/boundary vertical fibers. Owner: IntegralPointDeterminantMethods.

items.name: Taylor remainder on a nondegenerate real interval
items.statement: For f:ℝ→ℝ, n∈ℕ and a≠b, ContDiffOn ℝ (n+1) f (uIcc a b) implies that some c∈uIoo a b satisfies f(b)−taylorWithinEval f n (uIcc a b) a b = iteratedDeriv (n+1) f c · (b−a)^(n+1)/(n+1)!.
items.locator: Generic input to Bombieri–Pila selected proof path pp.1–6,14–17; Mathlib/Analysis/Calculus/Taylor.lean:348–363
items.note: Codex codex-a71f92 read the actual declaration statement at Mathlib pin 082e2d37e8b0463410cdb532e111cd43d5a66174. Set n=k−1 in bp-large-derivative-interval; a=b is a separate trivial case. This exactly supplies the generic remainder, not BP's scaled inequality. Tests: k=1; a=b bypass; f(x)=x^k. No Lean instantiation run. Eighth checkpoint (Claude Code, cc-7b31c4): the two adapters this note previously left open are now closed against the same pin, and the closure is written out in the report section “Eighth checkpoint: the Taylor endpoint adapter”. (i) The endpoint conversion needs no neighbourhood of the endpoint: Mathlib/Analysis/Calculus/IteratedDeriv/Defs.lean:70, iteratedDerivWithin_eq_iteratedDeriv (hs : UniqueDiffOn 𝕜 s) (h : ContDiffAt 𝕜 n f x) (hx : x ∈ s), has no interiority hypothesis, so with Mathlib/Analysis/Calculus/TangentCone/Real.lean:102, uniqueDiffOn_uIcc (hab : a ≠ b), it applies at the endpoint a ∈ uIcc a b whenever f is ContDiffAt there. With taylorCoeffWithin (Taylor.lean:62), taylorWithinEval_succ (Taylor.lean:87) and taylor_within_zero_eval (Taylor.lean:100) this rewrites taylorWithinEval f n (uIcc a b) a b as the ordinary Taylor sum ∑_{j≤n} (j!)^{-1} · iteratedDeriv j f a · (b−a)^j. (ii) The a=b case is taylorWithinEval_self (Taylor.lean:109), which gives both sides f a with zero remainder, so the a ≠ b hypothesis of the two cited Taylor lemmas is not a gap. What remains for BP2's scaled inequality is only the supremum step: ContDiffOn.continuousOn_iteratedDerivWithin (IteratedDeriv/Defs.lean:147) on an open U ⊇ uIcc a b, with IsOpen.uniqueDiffOn (TangentCone/Basic.lean:291) and the same conversion, makes iteratedDeriv (n+1) f continuous on uIcc a b, and IsCompact.exists_isMaxOn (Topology/Order/Compact.lean:246) with isCompact_Icc supplies the maximum. No Lean instantiation is claimed for any of this; the hypothesis actually used is C^{n+1} smoothness on an open set containing uIcc a b, which is stronger than the ContDiffOn hypothesis of the cited remainder lemma and is what BP2's polynomial and algebraic-branch setting provides.

items.name: Existence and uniqueness of polynomial interpolation
items.statement: For a field F, finite index set s, nodes v injective on s and values r, Lagrange.interpolate s v r evaluates to r(i) at v(i), has polynomial degree strictly less than #s, and is the unique polynomial with those properties.

items.name: Too many distinct roots force a polynomial to vanish
items.statement: For a polynomial p over a commutative integral domain, a finite type ι and an injective f:ι→R, if p.eval(f(i))=0 for every i and p.natDegree<Fintype.card ι, then p=0. Consequently a nonzero univariate polynomial cannot vanish on a finite set of more than its natural degree distinct elements.
